correct_text:
4.   Parse the ecdhSecretKey and mlkemSecretKey from the algorithm-
        specific data of the own secret key, and the ecdhPublicKey from
        the algorithm-specific data of the own public key, encoded in
        the format specified in Section 4.3.2
notes:
Step 9 of the decryption procedure in Section 4.2.4 uses ecdhPublicKey as
an input to multiKeyCombine():

   9.   Compute KEK = multiKeyCombine(mlkemKeyShare, ecdhKeyShare,
        ecdhCipherText, ecdhPublicKey, algId) as defined in
        Section 4.2.1

However, no step of the decryption procedure (steps 1-8) obtains
ecdhPublicKey. Step 4 parses only the secret components (ecdhSecretKey and
mlkemSecretKey). By contrast, the encryption procedure in Section 4.2.3
extracts this value explicitly in its step 3 ("Extract the ecdhPublicKey
and mlkemPublicKey components ... from ... pkComposite"); the decryption
procedure was written as a mirror of the encryption procedure but omits
the corresponding extraction step.

The value is uniquely determined and always available to the decryptor:
the recipient's ECDH public key is present in the public-key portion of
its own key material (Section 4.3.2.1) and can equivalently be recomputed
from ecdhSecretKey. There is therefore no ambiguity and no interoperability
impact; the numbered procedure is simply incomplete as written. The
corrected step 4 obtains ecdhPublicKey from the recipient's own public key
alongside the secret components it already parses, so that the value
referenced in step 9 is defined.

(Only ecdhPublicKey is required on the decryption side; mlkemPublicKey is
not, since neither ML-KEM.Decaps nor the key combiner in Section 4.2.1
consumes it.)
